name: Connors RSI(2) 2P: buy RSI2<5 above 200-day, exit above 5-day SMA
author: Larry Connors (ProRealCode port)
summary: Classic Connors RSI(2): in a long-term uptrend buy when 2-period RSI is deeply oversold and sell on a close above the 5-day SMA; claimed high win rate on indices.
notes: ProRealCode version is long-only, no stop (Connors used none).

name: Connors RSI(2) long/short with 200-day regime
author: Larry Connors / Cesar Alvarez (LuxAlgo summary)
summary: Buy RSI(2) dips above the 200-day SMA, short RSI(2) spikes below it, exit on a close back across the 5-day SMA.
notes: Source gives 10 (or 5 stricter) long and 90/95 short; mirrored thresholds via one param.

name: RSI(2) < 15, exit close above yesterday's high
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: Buy on the close when 2-day RSI is under 15 and sell when the close exceeds the prior day's high; claimed robust on SPY since 1993.
notes: No trend filter in the base version; the extra filter in the article is paywalled.

name: Connors cumulative RSI(2) < 35 above 200-day
author: Larry Connors / Cesar Alvarez
summary: Sum of the last two RSI(2) readings below 35 with close above the 200-day SMA; exit when RSI(2) rises above 65 (Short Term Trading Strategies That Work).
notes: Two-day cumulation as book default; 3-day variant not included.

name: Double 7's
author: Larry Connors / Cesar Alvarez (TradingView port)
summary: Above the 200-day SMA buy a 7-day closing low and sell a 7-day closing high; no stop.
notes: Faithful.

name: Connors R3 (RSI(2) falling three days)
author: Larry Connors (High Probability ETF Trading)
summary: Above the 200-day, RSI(2) drops three days in a row starting below 60 and ends under 10; exit when RSI(2) > 70.
notes: Aggressive version adds a second unit below entry - not expressible. Sources disagree whether the first drop starts above or below 60; QS 'below 60' used.

name: Connors TPS (Time/Price/Scale-in)
author: Larry Connors (High Probability ETF Trading)
summary: Above the 200-day, RSI(2) below 25 for two days -> buy, scale in on lower closes, exit when RSI(2) > 70.
notes: Scale-in 10/20/30/40% on lower closes not expressible; full position at first signal.

name: Connors Multiple Days Down / Up (MDD/MDU)
author: Larry Connors (High Probability ETF Trading)
summary: Buy when the market closed down 4 of the last 5 days, is above the 200-day and below the 5-day SMA; exit on close above the 5-day SMA (MDU is the short mirror).
long_entry: (close > sma(close, 200)) & (close < sma(close, 5)) & (((close < shift(close, 1)) + (shift(close, 1) < shift(close, 2)) + (shift(close, 2) < shift(close, 3)) + (shift(close, 3) < shift(close, 4)) + (shift(close, 4) < shift(close, 5))) >= 4)
short_entry: (close < sma(close, 200)) & (close > sma(close, 5)) & (((close > shift(close, 1)) + (shift(close, 1) > shift(close, 2)) + (shift(close, 2) > shift(close, 3)) + (shift(close, 3) > shift(close, 4)) + (shift(close, 4) > shift(close, 5))) >= 4)
notes: Booleans summed as 0/1. Aggressive scale-in not expressible.

name: Connors 3-Day High/Low method
author: Larry Connors (High Probability ETF Trading)
summary: Above the 200-day and below the 5-day SMA, buy after three consecutive days of lower highs and lower lows; exit on close above the 5-day SMA.
long_entry: (close > sma(close, 200)) & (close < sma(close, 5)) & (high < shift(high, 1)) & (shift(high, 1) < shift(high, 2)) & (shift(high, 2) < shift(high, 3)) & (low < shift(low, 1)) & (shift(low, 1) < shift(low, 2)) & (shift(low, 2) < shift(low, 3))
notes: QS rule text is paywalled; core idea (3 lower highs/lows) from the page, 200/5-day filters and 5-day exit are Connors' standard set for this book. Scale-in omitted.

name: IBS < 0.2 buy, IBS > 0.8 sell
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: Internal Bar Strength (close-low)/(high-low): buy the close when below 0.2, sell when above 0.8; claimed strong on SPY for two decades.
notes: Faithful; crypto daily bars are 24h so IBS is less meaningful than for equities with a real session close.

name: RSI(5) crosses below 30, hold N days (SPY and Bitcoin)
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: Buy when 5-day RSI crosses under 30 and exit after a fixed 1-10 day hold; claimed robust on both SPY and Bitcoin.
notes: Time exit approximated by the entry signal shifted by hold days; exits at the first such date even if re-triggered.

name: Williams %R(2) < -90, exit above prior high or %R > -30
author: Quantified Strategies rules (TradingView port)
summary: Short-lookback Williams %R oversold buy, exit on a close above yesterday's high or %R recovering above -30.
notes: Lookback adjustable 2-25 in source; default 2.

name: RSI(2) cross below 10, sell cross above 80
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: Buy when RSI(2) crosses below 10 and sell when it crosses above 80; tested on 9 timeframes of SPY, daily gave ~0.42% per trade and weekly the best friction tolerance.
notes: No trend filter; daily version taken.

name: RSI(2) oversold-level sweep above 200-day (sweet spot 5-16)
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: Tested every RSI(2) threshold 1-50 on SPY above its 200-day; RSI<9 (PF 2.59) and RSI<15 beat the textbook 30, with exits on RSI(2) above 50 or 70.
notes: Article also tests 3- and 5-day time exits; RSI recovery exit used here. Entry at next open matches the framework.

name: RSI 30-50 pullback in uptrend
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: In an uptrend (price above a rising 200-day) buy when 5-day RSI drops below 30 and sell when it reaches 50; SPY 81% winners, PF 3.
notes: 'Rising' 200-day approximated as above its value 20 days ago; the unspecified 'confirmation' step is dropped.

name: Short-lookback stochastic %K(2,2) < 25, exit above prior high
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: Buy when 2-period smoothed stochastic is below ~25 and exit when the close exceeds yesterday's high; 497 SPY trades, PF 2.33.
notes: %K(2,2) = 2-bar stochastic smoothed over 2 bars, mapped to stoch_d(n,2).

name: 5-day low and low of the range (IBS < 0.25)
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: Buy when the close is below the lowest low of the prior 5 days and IBS < 0.25; claimed ~0.46% per trade on SPY since 1993.
notes: Exit is paywalled; QS's standard exit (close above yesterday's high) assumed.

name: Keltner lower-band reversion, exit above typical price
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: Buy when the close is below a short Keltner lower band (6 days, 1.3 ATR) and sell when the close is above the typical price; SPY 77% win, PF 2.
notes: Best cluster 6-10 days and 1-1.5 ATR per source.

name: Williams %R pullback in 200-day trend (-80 dip, -50 re-cross)
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: Above the 200-day wait for %R(14) below -80, enter when it crosses back above -50; mirror short below the 200-day from above -20.
notes: Source exits are swing-low stop and partial profits at resistance; replaced by opposite extreme or trend break. 'Recent' dip window set to 5 bars.

name: CCI(9) below -90, exit above prior high
author: EdgeTools (Quantified Strategies CCI rules)
summary: Short-lookback CCI oversold buy below -90, exit when the close exceeds yesterday's high; QS reports 73% win, PF 1.9 on SPY.
notes: Optional SL/TP in script without defaults; omitted.

name: CCI Correction (bias + counter-trend dip)
author: StockCharts ChartSchool (after Donald Lambert)
summary: Long-term CCI sets the bias; in a bullish bias buy when short CCI dips below -100 then surges back above zero, mirror for shorts.
notes: Uses the page's daily substitute (100-day bias, 20-day signal). Bias is a latched state in the source (above +100 until below -100); approximated by sign of CCI(100). No exit given; Lambert-style exit used. Year approximate.

name: CVR3 VIX market timing (Connors/Landry)
author: Larry Connors / Dave Landry
summary: Buy equities when VIX closes 10%+ above its 10-day average (fear spike), sell when VIX falls back below the prior day's 10-day average; mirror for complacency.
notes: Original also needs the whole VIX bar above the MA and a VIX down candle (VIX OHLC not in vocabulary); uses EMA via PPO; designed for S&P not BTC. Year approximate.

name: Connors VIX Stretch
author: Larry Connors / Cesar Alvarez (Short Term Trading Strategies That Work)
summary: Above the 200-day, buy when VIX has been 5%+ above its 10-day average for 3+ days; exit when RSI(2) crosses above 65.
notes: Faithful except the target is BTC instead of S&P futures.

name: Stochastic Pop and Drop
author: Jake Bernstein / David Steckler
summary: With a 70-day stochastic bias and low ADX, buy when the 14-day stochastic pops above 80 on high volume (drop: below 20 for shorts); exit when it falls back through 50.
notes: Consolidation-breakout and PSAR trailing stop not expressed. Oscillator-momentum rather than reversion.

name: Bollinger %B with Money Flow confirmation
author: John Bollinger (Bollinger on Bollinger Bands)
summary: Buy when %B > 0.8 and MFI > 80 (strength confirmed by volume), short when %B < 0.2 and MFI < 20; Parabolic SAR stops.
notes: Band (20,2), MFI(14) and PSAR(0.02,0.2) are standard defaults; the page does not give them. Optional ADX<15 pre-filter and MACD pullback entry omitted. Assumes psar_dir is +1 long/-1 short.

name: The 'Last' Stochastic Technique (39-period)
author: StockCharts ChartSchool (Encyclopedia of Technical Market Indicators)
summary: Buy when 39-period stochastic %K crosses above 50 and the close exceeds the prior week's highest close; sell/short on the mirror.
notes: Prior week = 5 trading days (7 calendar days for crypto could be used). Slow %K (39,1) smoothing ignored; OBV confirmation optional and omitted. Year approximate.

name: RSI(50) crossing its 25-bar SMA
author: reees
summary: Moving-average crossover applied to a long RSI: long when RSI(50) crosses above its 25-bar SMA, flat when it crosses under.
notes: Oscillator momentum rather than reversion; appeared in Bitcoin RSI search results.

name: Raschke/Connors Holy Grail (ADX pullback to 20 EMA)
author: Linda Raschke / Larry Connors (Street Smarts), Konscio port
summary: In a strong trend (ADX > 30, 20 EMA above 50 EMA) buy the break of the high of a bar that pulled back to the 20 EMA.
notes: Stop-entry above the touch-bar high approximated by a close above it. Source has no exit; ADX-fade exit (from other ports) plus 50 EMA break used.

name: Connors RSI exit-from-oversold with fast/slow SMA (JoseMetal)
author: JoseMetal
summary: Above the slow SMA, after a close in RSI oversold the next close leaves oversold while still below the fast SMA -> long; exit on a close above the fast SMA; mirrored short; tested on BTCUSDT.
notes: Slow SMA and RSI length not stated on page; Connors defaults 200 and 2 assumed. Author prefers 4H; optional ATR SL/TP omitted.

name: Reversal Trading Ideas by Larry Connors (I11L): 7-bar low, RSI exit
author: I11L
summary: Buy a new 7-bar low (optionally only above the 55-day average), average down on further lows, exit when RSI closes above 70; no stop.
notes: Averaging-down not expressible. RSI length not stated, 14 assumed. 55-day filter is optional in the source and kept.

name: Connors RSI 25 / RSI 75
author: Larry Connors (High Probability ETF Trading) via Quantified Strategies
summary: Above the 200-day buy when 4-day RSI falls below 25, exit when RSI(4) rises above 75 (QS found 55 gives smaller drawdowns).
notes: Aggressive second unit at RSI<20 not expressible. Short side is the book's mirror (RSI4>75 below 200-day).

name: ConnorsRSI Pullbacks (Connors Research guidebook)
author: Connors Research
summary: Buy liquid stocks above the 200-day when ConnorsRSI(3,2,100) is very low via a limit order below the close; exit when ConnorsRSI rises above 70.
notes: ConnorsRSI needs a streak-RSI and 100-bar percent-rank of ROC, neither in the vocabulary; the limit-order entry below the close also needs intraday fills.

name: Bitcoin RSI(14) oversold cross with SMA 200/300 bull filter, 20-day hold
author: Sofien Kaabar (All About Trading)
summary: On daily BTC, when SMA200 > SMA300 buy RSI(14) crossing up through 35 and hold 20 bars (bear variant: SMA10<SMA20 short on RSI crossing down through 60); author warns the edge may be drift.
notes: Source RSI is EWM-smoothed (span 27); plain RSI used. 20-bar time exit approximated by shifted entry signal.

name: Turtle Soup Plus One (crypto port)
author: Linda Raschke / Larry Connors (Street Smarts), CryptoDataDownload port
summary: Day 1 closes at/below the prior 20-day low (which is 3+ days old); day 2 buy back at that old low; exit within 2-6 bars; mirror for highs; applied to Binance BTC.
notes: Buy-stop at old low approximated by a close back above it; stop below the new extreme approximated by a 5% stop; time exit by shifted entry.

name: Turtle Soup (20-day false breakout)
author: Linda Raschke / Larry Connors (Street Smarts)
summary: Fade a new 20-day low when the prior 20-day low is at least 4 sessions old: buy when price comes back above the old low; mirror at 20-day highs.
notes: Same-day reversal back inside approximated with the daily close; original uses trailing stops - replaced by a 5-day closing extreme exit and a 5% stop.

name: Connors %b strategy (3 days below 0.2)
author: Larry Connors (High Probability ETF Trading), EdgeTools port
summary: Above the 200-day, buy when Bollinger %b has been below 0.2 for three consecutive closes; exit when %b closes above 0.8; QS: strong on SPY/QQQ but few trades.
long_entry: (close > sma(close, 200)) & ((close - bb_lo(close, 20, 2)) / (bb_up(close, 20, 2) - bb_lo(close, 20, 2)) < 0.2) & ((shift(close, 1) - shift(bb_lo(close, 20, 2), 1)) / (shift(bb_up(close, 20, 2), 1) - shift(bb_lo(close, 20, 2), 1)) < 0.2) & ((shift(close, 2) - shift(bb_lo(close, 20, 2), 2)) / (shift(bb_up(close, 20, 2), 2) - shift(bb_lo(close, 20, 2), 2)) < 0.2)
notes: Band (20,2) from the StockSharp port defaults (doc.stocksharp.com 0968). Aggressive scale-in omitted.

name: Connors VIX Reversal II (RSI of VIX)
author: Larry Connors (StockSharp port)
summary: Go long equities when the 25-day RSI of VIX crosses above 61 (fear), short when it crosses below 42; hold 7-12 days.
notes: Originally for the S&P; time exit approximated by shifting the signal. Year approximate (Connors on VIX, mid-2000s).

name: Connors 'Spent Market Trading Pattern' (SMTP)
author: Larry Connors (StockSharp port)
summary: After a 10-bar low made on the widest-range bar of the last 10 that closes in its top 25%, buy a break of its high; trail a stop at successive lows.
long_entry: (low <= lowest(low, 9, 1)) & ((high - low) >= highest(high - low, 9, 1)) & ((close - low) / (high - low) >= 0.75)
notes: Buy stop one tick above the high approximated by next-bar entry; trailing stop at the highest low since entry approximated by a close below yesterday's low. Year approximate (Connors Investor Advisory era).

name: IBS 0.09/0.985 with 220-EMA filter and 14-bar max hold
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'IBS (Internal Bar Strength)'
summary: Buy extreme low IBS (< 0.09) only above the 220 EMA, exit when IBS exceeds 0.985 or after 14 bars.
long_exit: ((close - low) / (high - low) > 0.985) | shift(((close - low) / (high - low) < 0.09) & (close > ema(close, 220)), 14)
notes: Optional short side and min-distance pyramiding omitted; max-duration exit approximated by shifted entry signal.

name: Average High-Low Range + IBS reversal
author: StockSharp port of TradingView script
summary: Buy when the close has been below (20-day highest high - 2.5 x average daily range) for 2 bars and IBS < 0.2; exit on a close above the prior high.
long_entry: (close < highest(high, 20) - 2.5 * sma(high - low, 20)) & (shift(close, 1) < shift(highest(high, 20) - 2.5 * sma(high - low, 20), 1)) & ((close - low) / (high - low) < 0.2)
notes: Faithful to port defaults (Length 20, 2 bars, IBS 0.2).

name: Mean Reversion Pro (5/100 SMA with range position)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Mean Reversion Pro'
summary: For indices: buy when the close is below the 5-day SMA, in the bottom 20% of the day's range, yet above the 100-day SMA; exit when the close crosses above the 5-day SMA.
notes: Default is long only; short mirror listed as in source.

name: Mean reversion with incremental entry (5% from 30-SMA)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView script
summary: Buy when the low is 5%+ below the 30-period SMA (adding every further 1%), exit when the close returns to the SMA; mirror short.
notes: Incremental adds not expressible; single position.

name: Linear z-score mean reversion (enter |z|>2, exit |z|<0.2)
author: StockSharp port (MQL 'Linear Mean Reversion')
summary: Z-score of price vs its moving average over a half-life window: long below -2, short above +2, exit as z returns within 0.2 of zero.
notes: Fixed-point stop omitted.

name: Z-Score Buy/Sell (80-bar, 2.8 sigma, always in)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Z-Score Buy Sell'
summary: Long when the 80-bar z-score falls below -2.8, short when above +2.8, reverse on the opposite signal.
notes: Source default is 1-minute bars; cooldown of 5 bars omitted.

name: S4 IBS mean reversion with 3-candle exit
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'S4 IBS Mean Rev 3candleExit'
summary: Daily: buy after a bar with IBS <= 0.25; exit on the first close above entry, or after 3 candles if still losing.
notes: 'Close above entry' approximated by close above the previous close.

name: MFI exit-from-oversold with 1% target/stop
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'MFI Strategy with Oversold Zone Exit and Averaging'
summary: When MFI(14) climbs back above 20, place a limit buy slightly below the close; exit at +1% or -1%.
notes: Limit entry 0.1% below close not expressible; daily 1% TP replaced by MFI>80 exit (1% target is an intraday setting).

name: MFI level cross 40/60 (reversing)
author: StockSharp port (MQL 'MFI Level Cross')
summary: Long when MFI(14) drops to 40, short when it rises to 60, reverse on the opposite signal; 1% stop, 2% target.
notes: Source default is 4H candles with 1%/2% SL/TP; doubled for daily. Classic 20/80 included in params.

name: RSI(20) < 30 and close below lower Bollinger Band (reversing)
author: StockSharp port (MQL 'RSI Bollinger Bands')
summary: Buy when RSI is oversold and the close is under the lower band; sell short when RSI is overbought and the close is above the upper band; reverse on opposite signal.
notes: Source default timeframe 15m.

name: Bollinger RSI countertrend for SOL (weekdays only)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Bollinger RSI Countertrend SOL'
summary: Crypto countertrend: buy when price crosses back above the lower band with RSI(14) < 25 on weekdays, exit at the upper band; short above the upper band with RSI > 79, exit at the middle band or +3.5%.
notes: Built for SOL intraday; stop under recent lows approximated by 5%; short 3.5% target omitted. RSI<25 on the cross bar is rare on daily data.

name: Double Bollinger Bands (enter on 3-SD re-entry, exit at opposite 2-SD)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Double Bollinger Bands Signals'
summary: Long when the close crosses back above the lower 3-SD band, exit when it crosses above the upper 2-SD band; mirror short.
notes: Source default 5m candles.

name: Bollinger Bands mean reversion (below lower, exit above upper)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Bollinger Bands Mean Reversion'
summary: Textbook band reversion: buy a close below the lower (20,2) band, sell a close above the upper band; long only, no stop.
notes: QS notes this exit can trap you in downtrends (price never reaches the upper band).

name: Bollinger channel rebound (re-entry above lower band, exit at middle)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'strategy1'
summary: Buy when price that was below the lower band closes back above it; exit on a cross above the middle band or a touch of the upper band; stop below the channel.
notes: Stop 'below channel with 0.2 buffer' approximated by 5%.

name: Bollinger bounce reversal with MACD and volume confirmation
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Bollinger Bounce Reversal'
summary: Long when yesterday closed below the lower band and today closes back inside with MACD above signal and volume at/above average; mirror short; 2% stop, 4% target.
notes: Source is 5m with 2%/4% SL/TP; doubled for daily and opposite-band exit added.

name: Short-only 10-bar low pullback (IBS > 0.85 below 200 EMA)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Short Only 10 Bar Low Pullback'
summary: In a downtrend, short when the low breaks the 10-bar low but the bar closes near its high (IBS > 0.85); cover when the close drops below the prior low.
notes: Faithful to port defaults.

name: ATR 'sell the rip' mean reversion (short)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'ATR Sell the Rip Mean Reversion'
summary: Below the 200 EMA, short when the close spikes above a 10-bar smoothed (close + 1 x ATR20); cover on a close below the prior low.
notes: Faithful to port defaults.

name: Consecutive closes above prior high, short (mean reversion)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Consecutive Close>High[1] Mean Reversion'
summary: Below the 200 EMA, short after 3 consecutive closes above the previous bar's high; cover when the close falls below the prior low.
notes: Faithful to port defaults (threshold 3).

name: IBS short: IBS >= 0.9 and close above prior high
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Internal Bar Strength (IBS) Mean Reversion'
summary: Short a bar that closes at its high (IBS >= 0.9) and above yesterday's high; cover when IBS falls to 0.3 or below.
notes: Faithful to port defaults.

name: Connors TPS short side
author: Larry Connors (High Probability ETF Trading), StockSharp port
summary: Below the 200-day, short when RSI(2) has been above 75 for two days, scale in on higher closes, cover when RSI(2) drops below 30.
notes: Page lists only 'RSI and SMA filters and scaling'; thresholds are the book's TPS short mirror. Scale-in omitted.

name: Crypto MVRV Z-Score reversion
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Crypto MVRV ZScore'
summary: 252-day z-score of the market-value vs realized-value spread: long when it crosses above 0.382, short below -0.382.
notes: Needs realized cap (on-chain), not in the vocabulary.

name: Averaging down on RSI(10) < 33, exit above prior high
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Averaging Down' (after Quantified Strategies)
summary: Buy whenever RSI(10) is below 33, adding on each new signal, and exit when the close breaks above the previous bar's high.
notes: Averaging-down adds not expressible; single position.

name: Buy on 5-day low, sell above prior high
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Buy On 5 Day Low' (Quantified Strategies rule)
summary: Go long when the close falls below the lowest low of the previous 5 bars; exit when the close exceeds the prior bar's high.
notes: Port default is 5m candles; daily is the QS original.

name: Bollinger(10,2) + RSI(14)<30 long, exit at middle band
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Bollinger Bands Long'
summary: Buy a close below the lower 10-period band while RSI(14) is oversold; exit when price closes at or above the middle band.
notes: Faithful.

name: Gap-down reversal day
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Gap Down Reversal'
summary: Daily: when a session opens below the previous low but closes above its open (trapped sellers), buy; exit on a close above the previous high.
notes: Crypto trades 24/7 so true gaps are rare at the UTC daily open; signal will fire seldom.

name: Keltner channel fade (Kevin Davey)
author: Kevin Davey (StockSharp port)
summary: Simple volatility-channel reversal: buy when the close falls below the lower Keltner band (EMA10, 1.6 ATR), short when it closes above the upper band; always in.
notes: Source ATR period 14 vs EMA 10; vocabulary kc uses one period. Year approximate (Davey's Building Winning Algorithmic Trading Systems).

name: Reverse Keltner channel re-entry (weak-trend ADX filter)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Reverse Keltner Channel'
summary: When ADX < 25, buy price crossing back inside from below the lower Keltner band (EMA20, 2 ATR) and target the upper band; mirror short; stop at half channel width.
notes: Half-channel stop approximated by 5%.

name: RSI(8) 70/30 breakout with ADX filter
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'RSI & ADX Long Short'
summary: Momentum use of RSI: long when RSI(8) crosses above 70 and ADX(20) > 14, short when it crosses below 30; exit on the opposite RSI cross.
notes: Counter-example to reversion use of RSI; oscillator momentum.

name: RSI long-only with confirmed crossback (44 / 70)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'RSI Long Only with Confirmed Crossbacks'
summary: Buy when RSI(14) crosses back above 44 after dipping under it; exit when RSI crosses above 70.
notes: Port default is 5m candles.

name: RSI long: cross above 35, take profit at 55, stop below 30
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'RSI Long Position DAX 2h / Dow 1h'
summary: Buy when RSI(14) crosses up through 35; exit when RSI exceeds 55 or crosses back below 30.
notes: Built for DAX 2h / Dow 1h; daily used.

name: RSI 25/75 crossback, always in
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'RSI Strategy'
summary: Long when RSI(14) crosses back above 25, short when it crosses back below 75; reverse on the opposite signal.
notes: TradingView's built-in 'RSI Strategy' template logic; classic 30/70 in params.

name: Simple RSI stock strategy 1D (RSI5<30 above 200-day, ATR stop, staged targets)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Simple RSI Stock Strategy [1D]'
summary: Daily: buy when RSI(5) is below 30 and price is above the 200-day SMA; exit at a 1.5 ATR stop or staged 5/10/15% targets.
notes: Three staged targets collapsed to the middle 10%; ATR stop from entry approximated by a one-day 1.5 ATR drop.

name: Bar counter-trend reversal (3 falls into lower channel)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Bar Counter Trend Reversal'
summary: After 3 consecutive falling closes that reach the lower 20-period 2-SD channel, buy; after 3 rises into the upper channel, short; exit on the opposite signal.
notes: Channel type assumed Bollinger-style (length 20, multiplier 2); optional volume confirmation omitted.

name: Turnaround Tuesday on steroids
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Turn Around Tuesday on Steroids' (Quantified Strategies idea)
summary: On the first or second trading day of the week, buy after two consecutive down closes (optionally above the 200-day); exit on a close above the prior high.
notes: Week start mapped to Monday/Tuesday (dow 0-1); crypto trades on weekends so the 'Monday down' effect differs.

name: VIX spike (2 SD above 15-bar mean), hold 10 bars
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'VIX Spike Strategy'
summary: Buy the risk asset when VIX exceeds its 15-period mean by 2 standard deviations; exit after 10 bars.
notes: Port default is 5m; applied on daily VIX. Time exit approximated by shifted signal.

name: Z-Score normalized VIX (low-fear long)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Z-Score Normalized VIX'
summary: Average the 6-day z-scores of VIX, VIX3M, VIX9D and VVIX; go long when the combined score is below -1, exit when it rises back above -1.
notes: Only VIX is in the vocabulary; VIX3M, VIX9D and VVIX components dropped.

name: Z-Score RSI (RSI of price z-score crossing its EMA)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Z-Score RSI'
summary: Compute RSI(9) on the 20-bar z-score of price and trade crossings of its 15-bar EMA: long above, short below.
notes: Faithful to port defaults.

name: New 10-bar high with weak close (IBS < 0.15)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'New Intraday High With Weak Bar'
summary: Buy when the bar makes a new 10-bar high but closes in the bottom 15% of its range (failed push); exit when the close beats the prior high.
notes: Port default is 15m; daily used.

name: BTC chop reversal (EMA-ATR bands, RSI, MACD hist turn)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'BTC Chop Reversal'
summary: BTC reversal: long when the low pierces EMA23 - 4.4 x ATR55 with RSI(9) < 28, rising MACD histogram and a green bar; mirror short; tight TP/SL.
long_entry: (low < ema(close, 23) - 4.4 * atr(55)) & (rsi(close, 9) < 28) & ((macd(close, 14, 44) - macd_signal(close, 14, 44, 3)) > shift(macd(close, 14, 44) - macd_signal(close, 14, 44, 3), 1)) & (close > open)
short_entry: (high > ema(close, 23) + 4.4 * atr(55)) & (rsi(close, 9) > 68) & ((macd(close, 14, 44) - macd_signal(close, 14, 44, 3)) < shift(macd(close, 14, 44) - macd_signal(close, 14, 44, 3), 1)) & (close < open)
notes: Intraday 0.75%/0.4% TP/SL replaced by EMA-reversion exit and 4% stop on daily bars; sell-volume-spike filter omitted.

name: Bollinger excursion with RSI recovery (BB 25, RSI 33/60)
author: StockSharp port (MQL 'BB RSI Trailing Stop')
summary: Long when the low pierces the lower (25,2) band and RSI(14) crosses back above 33; short when the high pierces the upper band and RSI crosses back below 60; trailing stop.
notes: Point-based trailing stop replaced by middle-band exit and 5% stop. Default 15m.

name: Support/resistance with RSI and 200-EMA trend filter
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'DCA Support and Resistance with RSI and Trend Filter'
summary: Above the 200 EMA buy at the 50-bar support when RSI(14) < 40; exit at 50-bar resistance or RSI > 70; mirror short below the EMA.
notes: Support/resistance = 50-bar low/high; DCA sizing omitted; default 1m.

name: RSI(5) 30/70 mean reversion with golden-cross filter (Arthur Hill)
author: Arthur Hill (StockCharts SystemTrader)
summary: Only when the 50-day SMA is above the 200-day, buy RSI(5) dips below 30 and sell when RSI(5) rises above 70; ~78% winners on SPY/QQQ/IJR 2000-2016, best variant buys the cross back above 30.
notes: Base test 1; variant 3 (enter on cross back above 30) had the best CAR/MDD. Filter applied to the index in the source, to the asset itself here.

name: RSI(2) oversold/overbought with fixed 1- or 5-day hold (Alvarez study)
author: Cesar Alvarez
summary: Buy when RSI(2) < 20 and short when RSI(2) > 80, hold 1 or 5 days; shows mean reversion on the S&P only since ~1983-1995 (momentum before).
notes: A regime study rather than a full system; time exit approximated by shifted signal. Useful as a test of whether BTC is mean-reverting or momentum at the 2-day RSI horizon.

name: Raschke 'Anti' stochastic hook (7,10,3)
author: Linda Bradford Raschke (RoboForex summary)
summary: Slow stochastic line sets the trend; when the fast line pulls back toward it and hooks back in the trend direction without crossing, enter on the break of the signal bar; exit same/next day.
long_exit: shift((stoch_d(7, 10) > shift(stoch_d(7, 10), 1)) & (stoch_d(7, 3) > stoch_d(7, 10)) & (shift(stoch_d(7, 3), 1) < shift(stoch_d(7, 3), 2)) & (stoch_d(7, 3) > shift(stoch_d(7, 3), 1)) & (close > shift(high, 1)), 1)
short_exit: shift((stoch_d(7, 10) < shift(stoch_d(7, 10), 1)) & (stoch_d(7, 3) < stoch_d(7, 10)) & (shift(stoch_d(7, 3), 1) > shift(stoch_d(7, 3), 2)) & (stoch_d(7, 3) < shift(stoch_d(7, 3), 1)) & (close < shift(low, 1)), 1)
notes: Fast line = stoch_d(7,3), slow line = stoch_d(7,10) approximates the 7-10-3 stochastic. Break of signal-bar high approximated by close above it; stop below signal bar approximated by 3%; one-day hold.

name: Raschke 80-20 (momentum candle false break)
author: Linda Bradford Raschke / Larry Connors (Street Smarts)
summary: After a day whose body is 80%+ of its range, fade a next-day push beyond its close that comes back; target 50% of that candle, flat by end of day.
long_exit: shift((shift(open - close, 1) >= 0.8 * shift(high - low, 1)) & (low < shift(close, 1)) & (close > shift(close, 1)), 1)
short_exit: shift((shift(close - open, 1) >= 0.8 * shift(high - low, 1)) & (high > shift(close, 1)) & (close < shift(close, 1)), 1)
notes: Intraday re-entry approximated by the daily close back across the prior close; one-day hold instead of intraday target. Book version uses 'open in top 20%, close in bottom 20%'; RoboForex body-ratio version used.

name: Raschke Momentum Pinball (3-period RSI of 1-day ROC)
author: Linda Bradford Raschke / Larry Connors (Street Smarts), CryptoDataDownload port
summary: RSI(3) of the one-day price change below 30 marks a buy day (above 70 a sell day); enter next day on a first-hour breakout, exit by day 3.
notes: First-hour breakout entry and first-hour-range stop need intraday data; approximated by next-open entry, 2-day hold and 3% stop.

name: Whiplash (Street Smarts)
author: Larry Connors / Linda Raschke (Street Smarts), CryptoDataDownload port
summary: Buy at the close of a day that traded below yesterday's low but closed above its open and in the top half of its range; hold one day (mirror for sells).
notes: Source gives only buy rules explicitly; sell is the stated mirror. No exit given beyond 'one day forward'.

name: Smash Day reversal (close below prior low, then trade above its high)
author: Larry Williams pattern, CryptoDataDownload port
summary: Setup: today closes below yesterday's low; signal: the next day trades above the setup day's high -> buy (mirror for sells).
notes: Stop-entry above setup high approximated by a close above it; source gives no exit, so a fixed hold is used. Pattern originates with Larry Williams (Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading).

name: Wilder RSI failure swing
author: J. Welles Wilder (New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems)
summary: Bullish: RSI(14) dips below 30, rebounds to a fail point, makes a higher low above 30, then breaks above the fail point -> buy; bearish mirror above 70.
notes: Swing-point logic approximated with rolling windows (dip within 15 bars, last 4 bars above 30, RSI above its 8-bar high = fail-point break). No target in source; RSI 70 exit and swing-low stop used.

name: Lambert CCI +/-100 original rule
author: Donald Lambert
summary: Lambert's original use of CCI as a strength signal: long above +100 until it falls back below +100, short below -100 until it rises back above.
notes: Oscillator-momentum counterpart to the CCI fade entries.

name: CCI +/-200 fade to zero in non-trending markets
author: LuxAlgo (CCI mean-reversion variant)
summary: Inside a trading range (no trend), fade CCI excursions beyond -200/+200 back toward zero.
notes: 'Separate filter indicating no trend' set to ADX(14) < 20.

name: Lane stochastic %K/%D cross out of oversold in uptrend
author: George Lane
summary: With the trend up, buy when slow %K (14,3) crosses above %D after being at or below 20; exit when it reaches 80.
notes: Higher-timeframe trend filter mapped to the 200-day SMA; source gives no exits, opposite-zone exit used. Year approximate (1950s).

name: Cardwell/Brown RSI range rules: buy 40-50 dips in a bull range
author: Andrew Cardwell / Constance Brown (Technical Analysis for the Trading Professional)
summary: When RSI(14) has respected the bull range (no reading below ~40 for months), buy pullbacks into 40-50; a break of the range is a regime-change alarm.
notes: Source gives ranges only (bull ~40-90, bear ~10-60); 60-bar regime window and exits are assumptions.

name: Larry Williams Ultimate Oscillator oversold-then-centerline
author: Larry Williams
summary: Ultimate Oscillator (7/14/28 weighted buying pressure): buy after a dip below 30 when it rises back above 50 (the alternative trigger to the divergence break); sell on the mirror above 70.
long_entry: (lowest(100 * (4 * sma(close - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 7) / sma(max(high, shift(close, 1)) - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 7) + 2 * sma(close - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 14) / sma(max(high, shift(close, 1)) - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 14) + sma(close - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 28) / sma(max(high, shift(close, 1)) - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 28)) / 7, 10, 1) < 30) & cross_above(100 * (4 * sma(close - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 7) / sma(max(high, shift(close, 1)) - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 7) + 2 * sma(close - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 14) / sma(max(high, shift(close, 1)) - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 14) + sma(close - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 28) / sma(max(high, shift(close, 1)) - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 28)) / 7, 50)
long_exit: 100 * (4 * sma(close - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 7) / sma(max(high, shift(close, 1)) - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 7) + 2 * sma(close - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 14) / sma(max(high, shift(close, 1)) - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 14) + sma(close - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 28) / sma(max(high, shift(close, 1)) - min(low, shift(close, 1)), 28)) / 7 > 70
notes: UO built from sums as ratios of SMAs (equivalent). Divergence condition omitted; centerline trigger used. No exit in source; 70 used. Year = S&C publication.

name: MFI failure swing (Quong & Soudack)
author: Gene Quong / Avrum Soudack
summary: MFI(14) drops below 20, recovers, holds above 20 on the pullback and breaks its prior reaction high -> buy; mirror above 80 for sells.
notes: Swing logic approximated with rolling windows; no exits in source. Year approximate (MFI introduced late 1980s).

name: StochRSI oversold in 10/60 SMA uptrend, confirm on 10-day SMA break
author: Tushar Chande / Stanley Kroll (The New Technical Trader)
summary: In an uptrend (10-day SMA above 60-day), after StochRSI(14) dips below 0.2, buy when price breaks back above its 10-day SMA; mirror in downtrends.
notes: Interpretive guidance turned into rules; exit at the opposite StochRSI extreme is an assumption.

name: Scalping RSI(2) with 50/200 EMA trend and 1% trailing stop
author: Ninorigo
summary: Long when EMA50 > EMA200, price above EMA200 and RSI(2) is oversold; short on the mirror; exit on trailing stop or take-profit; suggested for 3-4h crypto charts.
notes: Page lists thresholds 90/10 apparently swapped; 10/90 used. 1% intraday trailing stop replaced by RSI extreme exit plus 3% stop on daily bars.

name: IFR2 (Brazilian RSI(2) setup)
author: jocker.soad
summary: Buy when price is above its EMA and RSI(2) is below 25; target the high of the bar two before the signal (popular 'IFR2' swing setup in Brazil).
notes: EMA length not stated; exit at the high of the last two bars approximates the 'antepenultimate bar high' level.

name: Four consecutive declining closes, exit above prior high
author: Quantified Strategies
summary: One of the strongest entry families in a 6,000-backtest ETF study: buy after four consecutive lower closes and exit on a rebound above the previous day's high (MTUM/SMH/QQQ ranked best).
notes: Article tests four exits (prior-high rebound, short MA, RSI recovery, 5-bar); prior-high rebound used. Entry at next open as in the study.

name: Williams VIX Fix bottom finder (CM_Williams_Vix_Fix)
author: Larry Williams / ChrisMoody
summary: Synthetic VIX from any price series, (22-day highest close - low) / highest close; buy capitulation when it exceeds its upper Bollinger band (20, 2) or 85% of its 50-bar high.
long_entry: (100 * (highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) >= sma(100 * (highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22), 20) + 2 * stdev(100 * (highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22), 20)) | (100 * (highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) >= 0.85 * highest(100 * (highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22), 50))
long_exit: shift((100 * (highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) >= sma(100 * (highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22), 20) + 2 * stdev(100 * (highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22), 20)) | (100 * (highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22) >= 0.85 * highest(100 * (highest(close, 22) - low) / highest(close, 22), 50)), hold)
notes: Indicator only (no exit); defaults 22/20/2/50/0.85 are the published script's standard inputs (page text does not list them). Fixed hold used, as in QS's WilliamsVixFix test. A crypto-native VIX substitute.

name: Levels of Fear (buy 5-7 sigma below the recent high)
author: AstrideUnicorn
summary: Plot levels 1-7 standard deviations below the recent highest price; the 5-7 sigma levels are suggested as contrarian buy zones of maximum fear.
long_entry: close <= highest(high, w) - k * stdev(close, w)
notes: Window default and the 'levels stability' smoothing are not on the page; sigma taken as stdev of price. No exit given (companion 'Levels of Greed' script handles exits); return to the window mean used.

name: Bitcoin leverage sentiment (z-score of longs/shorts ratio)
author: StockSharp port of TradingView 'Bitcoin Leverage Sentiment Strategy'
summary: 252-day z-score of BTC margin longs vs shorts: long when it crosses above 1.0, exit below -1.618; mirrored shorts.
notes: Needs exchange margin long/short position data (e.g., Bitfinex), not in the vocabulary. Funding_7d could be a proxy but would be a different strategy.

name: Guerilla Fear/Greed Index strategy (NAAIM + equity put/call)
author: calebsandfort
summary: Blend the NAAIM Exposure Index and equity put/call ratio into a 0-100 fear/greed index; buy when fear reaches a threshold and sell at greed; best on TQQQ.
notes: NAAIM and put/call data are outside the vocabulary. A crypto analogue would use fear_greed but that is a different index. Year approximate.
